summary:
Space Tourism is a pixel-art co-op game for 1–4 players in which your crew flies a real NASA-style mission to Mars. Players re-fly Mars Odyssey, Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter and MAVEN, each taking a role: navigator, engineer, comms or scientist.
First, the team builds one spacecraft together. Every part costs mass, power and budget, so a better camera means a bigger battery or a heavier rocket. Next, they pick a launch date (a window to Mars opens only once every 26 months) and fly the rocket through max-Q to orbit. During the cruise, everyone runs between stations to:
shield the ship from solar storms
steer around comet debris
keep the fuel from freezing
put out fires
repair panels on spacewalks
send science home while a Deep Space Network antenna is in view
At the end, they brake into Mars orbit. A report then explains why the mission succeeded or failed and compares it with what NASA actually did.
What it teaches: the core of real mission design. There is no perfect spacecraft, every choice is a trade-off, and fixing one bottleneck exposes the next. Along the way, players learn about orbital mechanics, launch windows, the rocket equation, space weather and radiation dose, and that spaceflight is teamwork.
details: When we made this game, we wanted it to be genuinely fun to play while also showing the player the real challenges and dangers of a space mission at every stage: designing the spacecraft, launching it, and surviving in space. We planned three levels, but in the time we had we finished one: the mission to Mars. To keep the game realistic, we built it on what actually happens in space. The hazards, the trade-offs and the mission details all come from real spaceflight and real NASA missions.
